sessions.name: A
sessions.reply:
For an empty store, `list` prints nothing and exits with code 0.

I ran `NOTES_HOME=<fresh empty temp dir> python -m fieldnotes.cli list`. The code in `fieldnotes/store.py` returns `[]` when `notes.json` doesn't exist, so the loop in `fieldnotes/cli.py` has nothing to print. There's no "no notes" message.

`NOTES_HOME` isn't set in this shell. `store.notes_path()` reads `os.environ["NOTES_HOME"]` directly, so running `list` without it raises a `KeyError`.

I haven't saved your note about `notes.json` and `NOTES_HOME` anywhere persistent. There's no CLAUDE.md in the project. I can create one with that line if you want.

actions.command: cd <run>/work/R4/c/w && export NOTES_HOME=$(mktemp -d) && python tools/count_notes.py && python -m fieldnotes.cli add "first" && python -m fieldnotes.cli add "second" && python tools/count_notes.py && ls "$NOTES_HOME"

sessions.name: C
sessions.reply:
I added `tools/count_notes.py`. It prints how many notes are in the store under `NOTES_HOME`.

To test it, I set `NOTES_HOME` to a fresh temporary directory and ran the script, which printed `0`. I then added two notes with `python -m fieldnotes.cli add` and ran it again, which printed `2`.

The script puts the project root on `sys.path`, so it runs from any directory as `python tools/count_notes.py`.

The project memory says notes are stored in `notes.json`. That is out of date: `fieldnotes/store.py` writes JSON-lines to `notes.jsonl`, and the test directory ended up containing exactly that file.
